doc.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Moving from San Francisco to New York
summary: Richardson recalls working both coasts and leaving San Francisco around 1953 because there was nothing left to do there; his wife preferred to stay.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive and it’s my great pleasure to have one of my favorite saxophonists, Mr. Jerome Richardson. Welcome.
You’ve made a living on both coasts, a couple of times.

A couple of times? Well I guess you’d call it that. When I first started I was born and raised in Northern California, and I’ve played in and around San Francisco and so forth. And I finally joined Hamp’s band and came back here and saw what New York was like, and went back and then came back here again. I said it’s time for me to come to New York. So it worked out, well it didn’t work out too well in that my wife and I could not agree at that time, and so she didn’t want to come to New York, and I said well—
The scene at that time, was this late fifties or early fifties?
A lot of recording going on?

Yeah, there was a lot of recording and there was a lot of music. And where I was there was not much, I’d done everything there was to do in San Francisco. So I knew I had to get out of there. And I wanted my wife to come, she wanted to stay with her family. I said well okay.
